# AnimatedIcon

Header: `winui/ui/media/AnimatedIcon.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/media/AnimatedIcon.hpp`.

An icon that animates between named visual states by playing segments of an [AnimatedIconSource](../rendering/animated-icon-source.md). It draws a fallback icon when it has no source it can show.

Going from state A to B plays the source's segment between the `AToB_Start` and `AToB_End` markers. Without those it looks for an `AToB` or `B` marker, then any marker named `ToB_End`. A numeric state name is read as a progress value. A segment plays for `duration * |to - from|`, and one shorter than 20 ms jumps straight to its end. A state set while a transition plays waits or interrupts as [queue_behavior()](#queue_behavior) says. The icon scales the source's natural size uniformly and is centered in its slot. App code or the owning control (such as [NavigationShell](navigation-shell.md#uinavigationshell) for its items) calls [set_state()](#set_state). The icon doesn't own the source.

Example: 
```cpp
static const ui::AnimatedFindVisualSource find; // stateless; one instance serves every icon
ui::Control<ui::AnimatedIcon> icon;

window.set_content(ui::Button{
    .width              = 75.0f,
    .accessibility      = {.name = "Search"},
    .on_pointer_entered = [&] { icon->set_state("PointerOver"); },
    .on_pointer_exited  = [&] { icon->set_state("Normal"); },
    .content            = ui::AnimatedIcon{.source   = &find,
                                          .fallback = ui::symbol_glyph(ui::Symbol::Find),
                                          .state    = std::string{"Normal"},
                                          .control  = icon},
});

// Imperative form of the same icon:
auto plain = std::make_unique<ui::AnimatedIconControl>();
plain->set_source(&find);
plain->set_state("Normal");
```

## `ui::AnimatedIcon`

An icon that plays a caller-supplied [AnimatedIconSource](../rendering/animated-icon-source.md) as its state changes, and draws a fallback icon when there is no source. Builds a [ui::AnimatedIconControl](#uianimatediconcontrol).

Example: 
```cpp
static const ui::AnimatedFindVisualSource find; // stateless; one instance serves every icon
ui::Property<std::string> state{"Normal"};

window.set_content(ui::Button{
    .width              = 75.0f,
    .accessibility      = {.name = "Search"},
    .on_pointer_entered = [&] { state = "PointerOver"; },
    .on_pointer_exited  = [&] { state = "Normal"; },
    .content            = ui::AnimatedIcon{.source   = &find,
                                           .fallback = ui::symbol_glyph(ui::Symbol::Find),
                                           .state    = state},
});
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::AnimatedIcon{
    .source, .fallback, .state, .queue_behavior, .foreground, .style, .margin, .width, .height,
    .min_width, .min_height, .max_width, .max_height, .horizontal_alignment,
    .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip, .accessibility, .on_pointer_entered,
    .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus, .on_key_down, .on_wheel, .control
}
```

Fields, in declaration order (designators must follow it):

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="uianimatedicon-source"></span>`source` | `ui::Binding<const ui::AnimatedIconSource*>` |  | The animation. Not owned, so it must outlive the built control. Null draws the fallback. |
| <span id="uianimatedicon-fallback"></span>`fallback` | `ui::Binding<ui::IconSource>` |  | The icon drawn while there is no source: a [Symbol](../rendering/namespace-ui.md#symbol), a glyph, a path or a picture. |
| <span id="uianimatedicon-state"></span>`state` | `ui::Binding<std::string>` |  | The visual state, such as "Normal", "PointerOver" or "Pressed". Each change plays the source's transition segment from the old state to the new one. |
| <span id="uianimatedicon-queue_behavior"></span>`queue_behavior` | `ui::Binding<ui::AnimatedIconQueueBehavior>` | `{ui::AnimatedIconQueueBehavior::QueueOne}` | What a change of [`.state`](#uianimatedicon-state) does while a transition still plays. QueueOne by default. |
| <span id="uianimatedicon-foreground"></span>`foreground` | `ui::Binding<ui::Paint>` |  | The icon's color: a fixed color or a theme resource. Unset uses the theme's text color. |
| <span id="uianimatedicon-on_pointer_entered"></span>`on_pointer_entered` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer moved onto the control. |
| <span id="uianimatedicon-on_pointer_exited"></span>`on_pointer_exited` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer left the control. |
| <span id="uianimatedicon-on_got_focus"></span>`on_got_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus arrived on the control, or on anything inside it, from outside it. A control with nothing focusable in it never gets focus, and never raises this. |
| <span id="uianimatedicon-on_lost_focus"></span>`on_lost_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus left the control and everything inside it. |
| <span id="uianimatedicon-on_key_down"></span>`on_key_down` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::KeyEvent&)>` |  | A key pressed while focus is on the control or inside it, before the control's own handling; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_key_down()](../tree/element.md#on_key_down)). |
| <span id="uianimatedicon-on_wheel"></span>`on_wheel` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::PointerEvent&)>` |  | A wheel turn over the control, before the control scrolls; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_wheel()](../tree/element.md#on_wheel)). |
| <span id="uianimatedicon-control"></span>`control` | `ui::ControlOut<ui::AnimatedIcon>` |  | Out: the handle that receives the built control. |

Plus the common fields `style`, `margin`, `width`, `height`, `min_width`, `min_height`, `max_width`, `max_height`, `horizontal_alignment`, `vertical_alignment`, `visible`, `tool_tip`, `accessibility` every spec carries ([conventions](../conventions.md#common-fields-on-every-spec)).

### build

```cpp
std::unique_ptr<Element> build()&&
```

Consumes the spec and returns the built [ui::AnimatedIconControl](#uianimatediconcontrol); the caller owns it.

## `ui::AnimatedIconControl`

Derives from `ui::Element`.

An icon that animates between named visual states by playing segments of an [AnimatedIconSource](../rendering/animated-icon-source.md). It draws a fallback icon when it has no source it can show.

Going from state A to B plays the source's segment between the `AToB_Start` and `AToB_End` markers. Without those it looks for an `AToB` or `B` marker, then any marker named `ToB_End`. A numeric state name is read as a progress value. A segment plays for `duration * |to - from|`, and one shorter than 20 ms jumps straight to its end. A state set while a transition plays waits or interrupts as [queue_behavior()](#queue_behavior) says. The icon scales the source's natural size uniformly and is centered in its slot. App code or the owning control (such as [NavigationShell](navigation-shell.md#uinavigationshell) for its items) calls [set_state()](#set_state). The icon doesn't own the source.

Example: 
```cpp
static const ui::AnimatedFindVisualSource find; // stateless; one instance serves every icon
ui::Control<ui::AnimatedIcon> icon;

window.set_content(ui::Button{
    .width              = 75.0f,
    .accessibility      = {.name = "Search"},
    .on_pointer_entered = [&] { icon->set_state("PointerOver"); },
    .on_pointer_exited  = [&] { icon->set_state("Normal"); },
    .content            = ui::AnimatedIcon{.source   = &find,
                                          .fallback = ui::symbol_glyph(ui::Symbol::Find),
                                          .state    = std::string{"Normal"},
                                          .control  = icon},
});

// Imperative form of the same icon:
auto plain = std::make_unique<ui::AnimatedIconControl>();
plain->set_source(&find);
plain->set_state("Normal");
```

### AnimatedIconControl

```cpp
AnimatedIconControl() = default
```

An icon with no source and no fallback: measures to nothing and draws nothing.

### source

```cpp
const AnimatedIconSource* source() const
```

The animated source being shown, or null (then the fallback glyph is drawn, if any).

### set_source

```cpp
void set_source(const AnimatedIconSource* source)
```

Sets the animated source. The icon doesn't own it, so it must outlive the icon. The current progress carries over to the new source. Updates layout and redraws.

### fallback

```cpp
const IconSource& fallback() const
```

The icon drawn while there is no source that can be shown (none set, or its `available()` is false): a glyph at its own size, anything else fitted into the icon's box. Empty by default.

### set_fallback

```cpp
void set_fallback(IconSource icon)
```

Sets the fallback icon. Updates layout and redraws.

### foreground

```cpp
const Paint& foreground() const
```

The icon's color: a fixed color or a theme resource. Empty, the default, uses the theme's text color.

### set_foreground

```cpp
void set_foreground(Paint color)
```

Sets the color the source draws in. Empty goes back to the theme's text color. Redraws.

### state

```cpp
const std::string& state() const
```

The state the icon was last asked for.

### set_state

```cpp
void set_state(std::string state)
```

Moves the icon to [`state`](#state), playing the source's transition into it (see the class description). Setting the state it already has does nothing.

### current_state

```cpp
const std::string& current_state() const
```

The state the last transition went to, which the next one starts from.

### progress

```cpp
double progress() const
```

The source's normalized progress (0..1) currently shown.

### is_playing

```cpp
bool is_playing() const
```

True while a transition segment is animating ([tick_override()](#tick_override) advances it).

### queue_behavior

```cpp
AnimatedIconQueueBehavior queue_behavior() const
```

What a [set_state()](#set_state) does while a transition plays. QueueOne by default.

### set_queue_behavior

```cpp
void set_queue_behavior(AnimatedIconQueueBehavior behavior)
```

Sets the queue behavior for subsequent [set_state()](#set_state) calls.

### last_segment

```cpp
const std::string& last_segment() const
```

The segment name the last transition resolved to, for example "NormalToPointerOver". Meant for tests.

### last_segment_start

```cpp
const std::string& last_segment_start() const
```

The start marker the last transition used (empty if it had none).

### last_segment_end

```cpp
const std::string& last_segment_end() const
```

The end marker the last transition used (empty if it had none).

### render_in

```cpp
void render_in(Renderer& renderer, const Theme& theme, const Color& foreground) const
```

Draws the icon like [render()](../tree/element.md#render), in [`foreground`](#foreground) instead of its own color. For a control that owns the icon and colors it from its own visual state.

### automation_role

```cpp
AutomationRole automation_role() const override
```

Exposed to UI Automation as an image.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

Uniform-scales the source's natural size into `available`, or measures the fallback glyph.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

Draws the source's current frame, or the fallback, in [foreground()](#foreground) or the theme text color.

### tick_override

```cpp
void tick_override(Duration delta) override
```

Advances a playing segment by `delta`, then starts the next queued state when it ends.

## Enumerations

### AnimatedIconQueueBehavior

```cpp
enum class AnimatedIconQueueBehavior
```

What a new state does while an [AnimatedIcon](#uianimatedicon) transition is still playing.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Cut` | a new state interrupts whatever is playing |
| `QueueOne` | the default: queue it behind the running transition |
| `SpeedUpQueueOne` | queue it, and play the running and queued transitions 7x faster |
